text:
Winnipeg won 3-2 in a game that was close to a coin flip on the chances: the Jets deserved to win 51 percent of the time, Pittsburgh 49. What decided it was a nine-minute burst in the third period, when the Jets scored three times and the Penguins answered once.

Ben Kindel's tip-in gave PIT a 1-0 lead midway through the second, on a chance that carried only a 10 percent probability of scoring. WPG owned the third, out-chancing PIT 2.03 expected goals to 0.97, and Alex Iafallo tied it at 4:43 with a wrist shot. Adam Lowry's backhand put the Jets ahead at 7:08 on a 7 percent look. Declan Carlile pulled PIT level at 8:53, but Cole Perfetti's snap shot restored the lead nine seconds later, at 9:02, and it held.

The goalies split the difference only slightly. Clay Stevenson stopped 29 of 31 and saved 0.8 goals more than expected, while Sergei Murashov stopped 32 of 35 and finished 0.12 below expected. PIT led in shot attempts, 65 to 58, but WPG put more on goal, 35 to 31, and Perfetti's four shots on goal led all skaters. Iafallo played only 10:24 yet was on the ice for 1.58 expected goals for and 0.33 against. Carlile and Kindel each had a goal and an assist for PIT, but neither could keep the Jets off the board in the third.
